spec: Task 005 stages 1 and 2: generate(mesocycle, cycle_one) -> microcycles 2..N, every one stamped with ENGINE_VERSION, for all five v1 strategies. Every rule column the engine reads is written out, null where the strategy does not read it. Dates are ISO here and whole days since 1970-01-01 in the core; each consumer converts. An expected load is target_weight_kg when it is an exact decimal, or target_weight_steps (x the exercise's increment, in the consumer's own arithmetic) when it is not. The output is compared whole: every cycle, session, exercise and set, in canonical order.

cases.name: fixture #1 — the owner's example: 40 kg 3x6 to 62.5 kg at cycle 11, deloads at 6 and 12
cases.note: 00 § Worked example. A deload consumes no step: cycle 7 resumes one step past cycle 5. It prescribes the last working load x 6000 bp (50 -> 30, 62.5 -> 37.5), 3 sets x 5000 bp with a tie to the fewer (1 set), and RIR 3 + 2 = 5 clamped to the rule's 4 and marked (01 FR-3.9).

cases.name: a block of 9-day microcycles: cycle 3 starts 18 days after cycle 1
cases.note: INV-25. 2026-10-05, 2026-10-14, 2026-10-23: no weekday anywhere. Three sessions on days 1, 4 and 7 keep their day indices in every cycle.

cases.name: mostly 7-day cycles with one 5-day cycle: every later start shifts, and day 7's session moves to day 5
cases.note: FR-3.1a, INV-25. Starts 10-05, 10-12, 10-19, then 10-24 — five days later, not seven. A session past the end of the shorter cycle moves to its last day, after the session already there (order 1): nothing is dropped. Loads tell the sessions apart.

cases.name: 24 cycles with deload_mode none: 24 working cycles and no deload anywhere
cases.note: FR-3.1b: 'none' is a first-class choice. 40 kg + 2.5 kg a cycle reaches 97.5 kg at cycle 24.

cases.name: a 2.5 % step (load_step_bp = 250) from a 140 kg squat prescribes 142.5 kg
cases.note: ADR-010 §3. A share of cycle 1's load per step, never compounded: 143.5 -> 142.5, 147 -> 147.5 (a tie would go lighter; 147 is 58.8 steps, nearer 59), 150.5 -> 150. The former 3 % gave 145.

cases.name: every second cycle a deload, and the final cycle too
cases.note: FR-3.1b. Deloads at 2 and 4, and 5 because final_cycle is set and the beat misses it. Cycle 3 is one step past cycle 1 (105). A deload multiplies the last working cycle: 100 x 0.6 = 60; 105 x 0.6 = 63 -> 62.5, for cycle 4 and for cycle 5. Two working sets deload to one. No RIR target stays none (INV-03).

cases.name: a manual deload on a fixed exercise keeps the warm-up and half the working sets
cases.note: FR-3.5, FR-3.9. Fixed holds 60 kg; the deload is the cycle's, so it applies. Four working sets keep two; the warm-up is not a counted set, so it stays, deloaded like the rest: 20 x 0.6 = 12 -> 12.5; 60 x 0.6 = 36 -> 35. RIR 2 + 2 = 4 fits the rule, so nothing is clamped.

cases.name: a target carried from cycle 1 outside its rule is clamped into it and marked
cases.note: INV-05: the engine never generates a set outside its rule. 10 reps on a 6-8 rule is 8; RIR 6 with a maximum of 4 is 4; was_clamped says why. Cycle 1 itself is the user's and is not rewritten.

cases.name: an imperial block stays on the 5 lb grid: 135 lb + 5 lb a cycle
cases.note: ADR-008, INV-02. 5 lb is stored as 2.267962 kg (numeric(10,6)) and 135 lb as 61.235 kg (numeric(9,4)). Expected loads are whole steps of the increment — 28, 29, 30, i.e. 140, 145 and 150 lb — written as steps because a product of 2.267962 has no short exact decimal.

cases.name: double progression 6-8 with a 2.5 kg step: 3x6@40 -> 3x7@40 -> 3x8@40 -> 3x6@42.5
cases.note: 01 §3.2 (b), task 005's criterion. The exercise moves as one: every set gains a rep until all are at the top, then the load steps and every set drops to the bottom. The range rides on each set.

cases.name: a rep step that would overshoot the top stops at it, and the load steps the cycle after
cases.note: Stage 2, decision 1. 8 + 3 = 11, then 12 rather than 14: the top is prescribed once before the load moves, and nothing is ever generated outside the range (INV-05).

cases.name: double progression through a deload: the deload takes no step, and the reps resume
cases.note: FR-3.9. Cycle 3 deloads cycle 2's 3x7@40 to 1x7 at 25 kg (24 -> 25 on the grid), RIR 2 + 2 = 4. Cycle 4 continues from cycle 2: 8 reps, then cycle 5 steps the load.

cases.name: a percent_1rm wave of 70/75/80 % of a 120 kg e1RM, tiled across the block, with a deload
cases.note: 01 §3.2 (c), stage 2 decision 2. Cycle 1 is the wave's first value; 90, 96 -> 95, then the deload at cycle 4 takes no wave step (95 x 0.6 = 57 -> 57.5, one set), and the wave resumes at 70 % (84 -> 85) and 75 % (90). The warm-up is held as authored, and deloaded like every set.

cases.name: percent_1rm on a bodyweight exercise prescribes the added load: e1RM x wave - body weight
cases.note: ADR-010 §1, stage 2 decision 3. An 80 kg lifter, e1RM 110 kg: 85 % is 93.5 kg, so 13.5 kg added -> 13.75 on a 1.25 kg grid; 80 % is 88 kg, so 8 kg added -> 7.5.

cases.name: percent_1rm on a bodyweight exercise with no body weight holds cycle 1's loads
cases.note: INV-07: no body weight, no guess. The strategy runs open-loop on cycle 1's added load (FR-3.2c).

cases.name: percent_1rm never prescribes a negative added load
cases.note: A 100 kg lifter at 80 % of a 110 kg e1RM is 88 kg, 12 kg under body weight: the added load is 0.

cases.name: rir_autoregulated descends from RIR 3 to 0 across the working cycles while the load climbs
cases.note: 01 §3.2 (d), stage 2 decision 4. Six working cycles (1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7): 3, 2.4, 1.8, 1.2, 0.6, 0 -> 3, 2, 2, 1, 1, 0. Deloads at 4 and 8 take no step: 105 x 0.6 -> 62.5 at RIR 4, 112.5 x 0.6 = 67.5 at RIR 2, one set each.

cases.name: a RIR exactly between two whole reps rounds to the higher
cases.note: Stage 2 decision 4: 3 -> 0 over three working cycles is 3, 1.5, 0, and 1.5 prescribes 2 — the side ADR-010's tie rule takes for loads.

cases.name: a per-set ladder [2, 1, 0] with max_rir 3 at target 3 prescribes 3, 3, 3, the first two clamped
cases.note: FR-3.8a, ADR-010 §2, task 005's criterion. 5 and 4 are clamped to the rule's 3 and marked; the last set is 3 + 0 and is not.

cases.name: the same ladder at target 1 prescribes 3, 2, 1, none clamped
cases.note: FR-3.8a, task 005's criterion: the ladder fits inside the rule, so nothing bends.

cases.name: a ladder's offsets go to counted sets only; a negative sum is clamped; a set past the ladder takes 0
cases.note: Stage 2 decision 5. Target 2, ladder [1, -3]: the warm-up keeps no RIR; the working sets are 2 + 1 = 3, 2 - 3 = -1 clamped to 0 and marked, and 2 + 0 = 2.
